option_description: Interpreted from the cache's bind/listen configuration: true when the instance listens on a publicly or broadly reachable interface (0.0.0.0, '* -::*', all interfaces) rather than loopback or a specific trusted private IP. The assessor derives this from the raw `bind` value; true is the exposed (insecure) state.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unauthenticated internet-exposed instance" (CVSS 9.8, T1190/T1133). It fires when data_store_publicly_routable is true AND default_user_unauthenticated is true, and again when data_store_publicly_routable is true AND protected_mode_enabled is false — a reachable interface is the precondition that turns missing auth into full unauthenticated network read/write.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the network interfaces Redis listens on and interpret loopback/specific-private (false) versus 0.0.0.0/all-interfaces (true).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: 1) "bind" 2) "127.0.0.1 -::1" or a specific private IP. Insecure (publicly routable): "0.0.0.0" or all interfaces.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check protected-mode, since binding all interfaces with protected-mode off is what actually makes the instance reachable unauthenticated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 1) "protected-mode" 2) "yes" (secure) or "no" (insecure).

option_description: Interpreted boolean over the composite Redis ACL/auth state: true when the built-in 'default' user is reachable with no credentials — shipped as 'user default on nopass ~* &* +@all' with no requirepass and no ACL password. True is the unauthenticated full-access (insecure) state.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unauthenticated internet-exposed instance" (CVSS 9.8, T1190/T1133). It fires when default_user_unauthenticated is true AND data_store_publicly_routable is true — a passwordless +@all default user reachable over the network is the classic mass-internet cache compromise (sessions/tokens dumped, FLUSHALL/CONFIG/Lua usable).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List ACL users and inspect the built-in default user's flags for the shipped passwordless full-access state.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Insecure: line 'user default on nopass ~* &* +@all'. Secure: 'user default on #<sha256-hash> ...' (password set) or 'user default off', plus least-privilege named users.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the default user directly to confirm whether a password is set and commands are narrowed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Insecure: flags include 'nopass'. Secure: 'passwords' array non-empty (a sha256 hash) and commands narrowed from '+@all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm no legacy single-password auth is set for the default user.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-empty value. Insecure: 1) "requirepass" 2) "" (empty — no password). Combine with ACL state to confirm the default user is truly unauthenticated.

option_description: Maps to Redis `protected-mode` (default yes): the safety net that, when bound to all interfaces with no password, accepts only loopback connections. true = 'yes' (secure); the condition fires on false ('no'), which on a reachable interface with no auth opens unauthenticated network access.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unauthenticated internet-exposed instance" (CVSS 9.8, T1190/T1133). It fires when protected_mode_enabled is false AND data_store_publicly_routable is true — disabling the safety net on an exposed, unauthenticated instance removes the last barrier to network read/write.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the protected-mode safety-net setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 1) "protected-mode" 2) "yes" (secure, protected_mode_enabled=true) or "no" (insecure, =false).

option_description: Raw Redis `bind` value (network interfaces the cache listens on), e.g. '0.0.0.0', '* -::*', '127.0.0.1 -::1', or a specific private IP. Source field the assessor interprets into data_store_publicly_routable; retained for context.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding the derived trigger data_store_publicly_routable in "Unauthenticated internet-exposed instance". The raw bind string is not itself an OR-condition in the policy — the interpreted boolean it produces is — so capture it verbatim to justify that derivation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the raw bind string verbatim for context behind data_store_publicly_routable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: 1) "bind" 2) "127.0.0.1 -::1" or a specific private IP. Insecure: "0.0.0.0" or all interfaces.

option_description: Raw Redis `requirepass` value — legacy single-password auth for the default user. Empty ('') means no password via this mechanism; combined with the ACL state it determines default_user_unauthenticated. Retained for context (ACL-based auth may set the default password instead).
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding default_user_unauthenticated in "Unauthenticated internet-exposed instance". The raw value is not a direct OR-condition; the interpreted unauthenticated boolean it helps derive is. Capture it to evidence whether legacy auth is set.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the legacy single-password auth value; combine with ACL state to derive default_user_unauthenticated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-empty value. Insecure: 1) "requirepass" 2) "" (empty — no password). When ACLs are used the default user password may be set via ACL instead.

option_description: Whether client traffic to the store is served over a TLS listener (Redis tls-port set non-zero with tls-cert-file/tls-key-file present). When false, session IDs and bearer tokens travel as plaintext RESP, readable by any on-path attacker. Secure value is true.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext transport interception" (CVSS 7.4, T1040/T1557/T1562.010/T1048.003). It fires when flow_tls_encrypted is false AND tls_only_transport is false — no TLS listener means sessions/tokens cross the wire in cleartext and can be harvested and replayed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether a TLS listener is enabled (non-zero TLS port).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-zero TLS port. Insecure: "0" (TLS disabled).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a server certificate is configured, since TLS cannot be served without it even when tls-port is set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a path to a server certificate (with tls-key-file/tls-ca-cert-file also set). Insecure: empty.

option_description: Whether the cleartext listener is disabled so clients can connect ONLY over TLS (Redis port 0 with tls-port set). When false, the cleartext port (e.g. 6379) accepts unencrypted connections alongside any TLS port, leaving plaintext interception possible. Secure value is true.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext transport interception" (CVSS 7.4, T1040/T1557). It fires when tls_only_transport is false AND flow_tls_encrypted is false — leaving the cleartext port open means an attacker can intercept (or downgrade clients to) the unencrypted listener even if TLS is also offered.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the cleartext TCP listener is disabled (port 0).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure (TLS-only): 1) "port" 2) "0". Insecure: "6379" with no TLS, meaning cleartext is accepted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the TLS port is set, so disabling the cleartext port still leaves clients a path.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-zero TLS port paired with port 0. Insecure: "0".

option_description: Whether the TLS listener permits legacy protocol versions (TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1) — the downgradeable variant of the cleartext exposure. Interpreted from the Redis tls-protocols directive; the assessor sets true when TLSv1.0/1.1 are allowed. Secure value is false.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Cleartext transport interception" (CVSS 7.4, T1040/T1557). It fires on its own when weak_tls_versions_enabled is true — permitting TLSv1.0/1.1 lets an attacker force a downgrade to weak-cipher / breakable TLS and recover sessions/tokens.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the allowed TLS protocol versions and interpret whether legacy versions are permitted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: "TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3". Insecure (weak versions enabled): includes TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1.

option_description: The lowest TLS protocol version accepted on the encrypted transport, derived from the Redis tls-protocols directive. TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 are downgradeable and weak-cipher-prone; secure values are TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Cleartext transport interception" (CVSS 7.4, T1040/T1557). It fires when min_tls_version is in [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1] — a minimum at a legacy version is the same downgrade exposure carried as an explicit enum alongside weak_tls_versions_enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the tls-protocols directive and interpret the lowest enabled version.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: "TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3" (min TLSv1.2/1.3). Insecure: includes TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 (min at a legacy version).

option_description: Whether the TLS listener negotiates only strong cipher suites (no aNULL/eNULL/RC4/MD5/export). Interpreted from the Redis tls-ciphers/tls-ciphersuites directives rather than substring-matching the raw list. Secure value is true.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Cleartext transport interception" (CVSS 7.4, T1040/T1557). It fires on its own when cipher_suites_strong_only is false — negotiable weak/NULL/export ciphers let an on-path attacker break or strip the encryption protecting sessions/tokens.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the TLSv1.2-and-below cipher list and interpret whether only strong suites are negotiable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Interpret: true when no aNULL/eNULL/RC4/MD5/export suites are negotiable (e.g. a hardened HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5-style list). false when weak suites are permitted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the TLSv1.3 cipher suites to confirm the 1.3 suite list is also strong.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns the configured TLSv1.3 ciphersuites; confirm only strong suites are present.

option_description: Whether the cache writes in-memory state to disk via RDB snapshots (the 'save' schedule) or the append-only file (appendonly yes). When true for a session/token tier, transient secrets are durably written to disk — the firing (insecure) value for this transient-secret store.
security_impact: The shared trigger for "Sensitive transient data exposed via persistence" (CVSS 7.1, T1005/T1552). It fires when persistence_enabled is true AND encrypted_at_rest is false, and again when persistence_enabled is true AND dump_files_world_readable is true — persistence is the precondition that turns transient sessions/tokens into an at-rest exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether append-only-file persistence is enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "yes" or "no". If yes (or save is set), confirm the dir (CONFIG GET dir) is on encrypted storage with restricted file permissions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the RDB snapshot schedule — the other persistence mechanism.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A schedule like "3600 1 300 100 60 10000" (snapshotting on, persistence_enabled=true) or "" (disabled). When set, verify dir + file permissions + disk encryption.

option_description: Whether persisted RDB/AOF data is protected by at-rest encryption. Redis has no built-in at-rest encryption, so this is satisfied only by an encrypted/restricted volume or filesystem hosting CONFIG GET dir. False (no at-rest encryption while persistence is on) fires the exposure: cleartext dump.rdb/appendonly files leak sessions and tokens.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Sensitive transient data exposed via persistence" (CVSS 7.1, T1005/T1552). It fires when encrypted_at_rest is false AND persistence_enabled is true — an unencrypted dump.rdb/appendonly file is a cleartext copy of the very secrets the cache held transiently.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Identify the persistence directory whose underlying volume must be encrypted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns the directory holding dump.rdb/appendonly files; this is the path whose volume must be confirmed encrypted at rest.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the filesystem/volume hosting the persistence dir is encrypted at rest (LUKS, cloud volume encryption, etc.); Redis itself provides no at-rest encryption.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Encrypted volume/filesystem evidence (LUKS, EBS/PD/Azure-disk encryption attestation) => encrypted_at_rest=true. No encryption on the dir's volume => false.

option_description: Whether the persistence directory and its dump.rdb/appendonly files carry broad (world/group-readable) permissions, letting any local user or co-tenant read the persisted secrets. Positive-insecure complement of the config-files-not-world-readable attestation; true fires the exposure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Sensitive transient data exposed via persistence" (CVSS 7.1, T1005/T1552). It fires when dump_files_world_readable is true AND persistence_enabled is true — broadly-readable dumps expose persisted sessions/tokens to any host-local reader even when disk encryption guards only against stolen disks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Find the persistence directory, then inspect file permissions on it and its dump.rdb/appendonly files.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns the persistence directory path to inspect for permissions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List permissions on the dump/AOF files in the persistence directory.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: World- or group-readable (e.g. 0644 / 0640 to a broad group) => dump_files_world_readable=true. Owner-only (e.g. 0600 / 0640 to redis only) => false.

option_description: Whether at-rest protection rests solely on full-disk/volume encryption (which guards stolen-disk/offline access) without file-permission restriction or app-layer secret handling. Context that sharpens the dump_files_world_readable finding — disk encryption alone does not stop a host-local reader. Not itself a trigger.
security_impact: Contextual evidence (CONTEXTUAL_EVIDENCE) supporting "Sensitive transient data exposed via persistence"; it is not one of the policy's OR-conditions. It explains residual risk: disk encryption alone leaves a world-readable dump readable to any logged-in host user.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether at-rest protection is full-disk/volume encryption only, with no file-permission restriction or application-layer secret handling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: True if disk/volume encryption is the sole control (no restrictive file perms, no app-layer handling); false if file-permission restriction or app-layer protection is also in place.

option_description: Whether the running Redis engine has been patched within the remediation SLA to a release fixing known critical CVEs — notably CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell), the Lua use-after-free enabling sandbox escape to native RCE. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "RediShell Lua sandbox escape to RCE" (CVSS 10.0, T1059.011/T1190). It fires when cache_patched_within_sla is false AND scripting_restricted_for_app_users is false — an unpatched engine with Lua scripting reachable by app users leaves the use-after-free sandbox-escape path open.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running engine version and compare against the fixed release for CVE-2025-49844.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Compare redis_version against the fixed release for CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell). At/after the fixed cutoff within SLA => true; pre-fix => false.

option_description: Whether EVAL/EVALSHA/SCRIPT/FCALL (the Lua scripting attack surface) is removed from the credentials applications use — i.e. app/named ACL users carry '-@scripting' rather than inheriting the default user's '+@all'. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false.
security_impact: Shared OR-trigger for "RediShell Lua sandbox escape to RCE" (CVSS 10.0, T1059.011/T1190). It fires when scripting_restricted_for_app_users is false AND cache_patched_within_sla is false, and again when scripting_restricted_for_app_users is false AND unpatched_known_rce_cve is true — leaving scripting reachable keeps the RediShell sandbox-escape surface available.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether scripting commands are restricted for the app credentials by inspecting the relevant ACL user.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure app users carry '-@scripting' (or EVAL/SCRIPT excluded) so the Lua attack surface is removed; insecure when scripting remains in the command set.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List all ACL users and verify named app users (not just default) exclude scripting commands.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-app named users carrying -@scripting => true. App credentials inheriting +@all / scripting commands => false.

option_description: Interpreted boolean: the running redis_version is at or below the vulnerable range for a known critical RCE CVE that remains unremediated — specifically CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell). Secure value is false; the exposure fires when true.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "RediShell Lua sandbox escape to RCE" (CVSS 10.0, T1059.011/T1190). It fires when unpatched_known_rce_cve is true AND scripting_restricted_for_app_users is false — a vulnerable version with scripting reachable is the exploitable RediShell configuration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running engine version and derive whether it sits at/below the vulnerable, unremediated range.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Compare redis_version against the CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell) fixed-version cutoff for the deployed branch. At/below vulnerable range and unremediated => true.

option_description: Raw running engine version string from 'redis-cli INFO server | grep redis_version'. Context only — interpreted against the CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell) fixed-release cutoff to derive cache_patched_within_sla / unpatched_known_rce_cve. Not pattern-matched directly.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding the patch-currency derivations in "RediShell Lua sandbox escape to RCE". The raw version string is not itself an OR-condition; the interpreted patch booleans it produces are. Capture it to evidence the version verdict.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the raw engine version verbatim for context behind the patch-currency derivations.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A line like 'redis_version:7.4.1' — recorded verbatim; feeds cache_patched_within_sla / unpatched_known_rce_cve.

option_description: Whether app/named ACL users carry -@dangerous/-@admin so destructive/administrative commands (FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB, KEYS, CONFIG, SHUTDOWN, DEBUG) are not grantable to them. True only when those categories are excluded from the credentials apps actually use; false fires the exposure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Over-privileged / destructive command access" (CVSS 8.1, T1485). It fires when dangerous_commands_acl_restricted is false AND dangerous_commands_renamed_or_disabled is false — destructive commands reachable by neither ACL nor rename means a compromised app credential can FLUSHALL/CONFIG/KEYS at will.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List the dangerous command category, then verify app users carry -@dangerous/-@admin.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lists the dangerous category (FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB, KEYS, CONFIG, SHUTDOWN, DEBUG, SAVE, BGSAVE, MONITOR, REPLICAOF, MIGRATE, RESTORE, CLIENT, INFO). App users should carry -@dangerous / -@admin so these are not grantable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List ACL users and confirm app credentials exclude the dangerous/admin categories.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Dangerous/admin categories excluded for app users (e.g. '... -@dangerous -@admin') => true. App users with +@all / no exclusions => false.

option_description: Whether dangerous commands are neutralised at the engine level via the legacy `rename-command` mechanism (e.g. `rename-command FLUSHALL ""` to disable, or renamed to an unguessable token) for CONFIG/FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB/KEYS/DEBUG/SHUTDOWN. False (all commands available under normal names) is the secondary trigger.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Over-privileged / destructive command access" (CVSS 8.1, T1485). It fires when dangerous_commands_renamed_or_disabled is false AND dangerous_commands_acl_restricted is false — AND-ed with the ACL facet, it means destructive commands are reachable by neither defence.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the redis config for rename-command directives neutralising destructive commands (CONFIG GET does not list renamed commands).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: lines like 'rename-command FLUSHALL ""' (disabled) or renamed to an unguessable token => true. Insecure: no rename-command lines => false.

option_description: Whether least-privilege named users exist for applications (each scoped to the keys/commands it needs) rather than every client authenticating as the all-powerful built-in `default` user (`+@all`). Interpreted from `ACL LIST` / a configured `aclfile`. False (only the single full-access default user) fires this exposure on its own.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Over-privileged / destructive command access" (CVSS 8.1, T1485). It fires on its own when least_privilege_access_enforced is false — if every client is the +@all default user, any compromised credential inherits FLUSHALL/CONFIG/KEYS.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List ACL users and check whether per-app scoped named users exist or only the built-in default user is present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-app scoped named users present (e.g. 'user app-read on ... ~app:* +@read') => true. Only 'user default on ... +@all' => false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether an external ACL file defining least-privilege users is configured.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a configured path (e.g. /etc/redis/users.acl). Insecure: empty (no external ACL file; rely on a single default user).

option_description: Raw `CONFIG GET aclfile` value — path to the external ACL file defining least-privilege named users. Empty means only the built-in default user exists; supports deriving least_privilege_access_enforced. Context only, not a trigger.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding least_privilege_access_enforced in "Over-privileged / destructive command access". The raw path is not itself an OR-condition; the interpreted least-privilege boolean it supports is. Capture it to evidence whether scoped users are even defined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the aclfile path (or empty) for context behind least_privilege_access_enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a configured path. Insecure: empty (no external ACL file; rely on a single default user).

option_description: Interpreted from the Redis 'maxmemory' config key: true when a sized non-zero memory cap is configured (e.g. 4gb), false when maxmemory is 0/unset (unbounded growth). With no cap a flood of writes drives the host to OOM, taking down the hot-data tier fronting auth/session state.
security_impact: The dominant OR-trigger for "Memory-exhaustion denial of service" (CVSS 6.5, T1499.003/T1499.001). It fires on its own when maxmemory_limit_set is false, and also pairs with maxmemory_policy=noeviction — an unbounded cache lets an attacker or runaway client write until the host OOMs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured memory cap and interpret zero (unbounded) versus a sized limit.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-zero byte limit (maxmemory_limit_set=true). Insecure: "0" (unbounded, =false).

option_description: The Redis 'maxmemory-policy' eviction policy applied when the memory limit is reached. 'noeviction' returns errors on writes once full rather than evicting — when paired with an unset maxmemory and TTL-bearing session data this is an availability hazard. A volatile-*/allkeys-* policy with a set maxmemory bounds growth.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Memory-exhaustion denial of service" (CVSS 6.5, T1499.003/T1499.001). It fires when maxmemory_policy eq 'noeviction' AND maxmemory_limit_set is false — a noeviction policy with no cap means a write flood drives OOM rather than bounded eviction.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the active eviction policy and evaluate against whether maxmemory is set and keys carry TTLs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns the active policy (noeviction|allkeys-lru|volatile-lru|allkeys-lfu|volatile-ttl|...). 'noeviction' is the firing value; an allkeys-*/volatile-* policy paired with a set maxmemory bounds growth.

option_description: Raw value of the Redis 'maxmemory' config key (e.g. "0" for unbounded, or a byte limit like "4gb"). Retained as context; the load-bearing trigger is the interpreted boolean maxmemory_limit_set derived from this value.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding maxmemory_limit_set in "Memory-exhaustion denial of service". The raw value is not itself an OR-condition; the interpreted cap boolean it produces is. Capture it to evidence whether a cap exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the raw maxmemory value verbatim for context behind maxmemory_limit_set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a non-zero byte limit. Insecure: "0" (unbounded).

option_description: Interpreted: Redis has no durable log destination — `logfile` is empty AND syslog is not enabled — so operational/audit logs go to volatile stdout only. Derived from `CONFIG GET logfile` (empty) together with the absence of `syslog-enabled yes`; true means there is no persistent audit trail.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Insufficient audit logging" (CVSS 5.3, T1562.012/T1562). It fires on its own when persistent_logging_absent is true — stdout-only logging leaves no durable record of who connected, blinding detection of scraping, brute-force, and DoS.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the log destination; an empty logfile with no syslog means volatile stdout-only logging.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a file path (and/or syslog-enabled yes). Insecure: empty with no syslog (persistent_logging_absent=true).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether syslog forwarding is enabled, since syslog can provide durable off-box retention even with an empty logfile.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "yes" provides a durable path; "no" with an empty logfile => persistent_logging_absent=true.

option_description: Raw Redis `logfile` config value (`CONFIG GET logfile`). Empty with no syslog means logs are emitted to stdout only (volatile). Retained for context to derive persistent_logging_absent.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding persistent_logging_absent in "Insufficient audit logging". The raw value is not itself an OR-condition; the interpreted no-durable-log boolean it helps derive is. Capture it to evidence the log destination.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the raw logfile path (or empty) for context behind persistent_logging_absent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a file path (and/or syslog-enabled yes). Insecure: empty with no syslog.

option_description: Raw Redis `syslog-enabled` config value. When true, Redis ships logs to syslog (which can forward off-box for durable retention). Used together with `logfile` to derive persistent_logging_absent.
security_impact: Context (DERIVATION_INPUT) feeding persistent_logging_absent in "Insufficient audit logging". The raw value is not itself an OR-condition; it combines with logfile to derive the no-durable-log boolean. Capture it to evidence whether off-box log retention exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read syslog-enabled and combine with logfile to derive persistent_logging_absent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "yes" (logs to syslog, can forward off-box) or "no". Combine with an empty logfile to conclude no durable log.

option_description: Redis `slowlog-log-slower-than` threshold in microseconds. A negative value (-1) disables the slow-query log — the closest Redis has to command-level audit — removing any record of abusive/expensive commands (KEYS, big SORT, repeated AUTH failures) that signal scraping/brute-force/DoS. Secure is a positive threshold (e.g. 10000); insecure (firing) is < 0.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Insufficient audit logging" (CVSS 5.3, T1562.012/T1562). It fires on its own when slowlog_log_slower_than lt 0 — a disabled slowlog (-1) removes visibility into abusive/expensive commands.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the slow-query log threshold; a negative value disables it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a positive integer (microseconds, e.g. 10000). Insecure: "-1" (slowlog disabled, firing).

option_description: Whether a durable audit trail of access (who connected, when) is captured and retained for this component. Supporting context for the audit-logging posture; not itself the trigger for this exposure.
security_impact: Contextual evidence (CONTEXTUAL_EVIDENCE) supporting "Insufficient audit logging"; it is not one of the policy's OR-conditions (persistent_logging_absent and slowlog_log_slower_than<0 are what fire). It records whether connection/access events are durably retained.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether connection/access events are durably captured and retained for the cache.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that connect/auth events are written to a durable, retained destination => true; volatile/no capture => false.

option_description: Whether security-relevant events (authentication failures, privileged/abusive commands) are fully captured in logs. Supporting context; the volatile-stdout and disabled-slowlog conditions are what actually fire the exposure.
security_impact: Contextual evidence (CONTEXTUAL_EVIDENCE) supporting "Insufficient audit logging"; it is not one of the policy's OR-conditions. It records whether auth failures and privileged-command events are captured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether auth failures and privileged/abusive command events are fully captured in the logs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Complete coverage of auth-failure and privileged-command events in retained logs => true; gaps or absence => false.

option_description: Whether logs are shipped to and retained on a separate system (off-box, tamper-resistant). Supporting context for the durability of any audit trail; relevant to whether stdout-only logging is recoverable.
security_impact: Contextual evidence (CONTEXTUAL_EVIDENCE) supporting "Insufficient audit logging"; it is not one of the policy's OR-conditions. It records whether logs survive off-box (tamper-resistant retention) independent of the firing conditions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether logs are forwarded to and retained on a separate, off-box system.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Off-box retention present (syslog/log-shipper to a separate, tamper-resistant store) => true; local/volatile only => false.
